chunks: Whatever is in it from Yaḥyā ibn Abī ʿImrān, I have narrated it from Muḥammad ibn ʿAlī Mājīlawayh—may Allah be pleased with him—from ʿAlī ibn Ibrāhīm, from his father, from Yaḥyā ibn Abī ʿImrān,
and he was a student of Yūnus ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān.

key_terms.تِلْمِيذَ يُونُسَ بْنِ عَبْدِ الرَّحْمَن: A student of Yūnus ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān; a brief biographical identifier of the transmitter.
key_terms.رَوَيْتُهُ: I transmitted it; indicates the author’s own route of narration.
key_terms.يَحْيَى بْنِ أَبِي عِمْرَانَ: A named transmitter whose chain is being clarified.

ai.seo_question: What is the transmission chain to Yaḥyā ibn Abī ʿImrān in Man Lā Yaḥḍuruhu al-Faqīh?
ai.summary: This passage clarifies the sanad/isnad through which the author transmits reports from Yaḥyā ibn Abī ʿImrān. It also briefly identifies him biographically as a student of Yūnus ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān, helping situate him within the transmission network of Shia hadith.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Everything in this book that is narrated from Yahya ibn Abi 'Imran has been transmitted by me from Muhammad ibn Ali Majilawayh - may Allah (swt) be pleased with him - from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Yahya ibn Abi 'Imran.
He was a student of Yunus ibn 'Abd Al-Rahman.
